verdict: Passed independent analytical review and exact example rerun, within the stated restricted scope.

analytical_checks.result: The original-measure decomposition T^m=sum_alpha B_alpha^m psi_i,alpha psi_j,alpha follows from fiber orthonormality with the original coarse pi retained. Entrywise nonnegativity of each B_alpha^2 and actual nonnegative cubic moments prove coarse domination for finite simple graphs of maximum degree three and independent positive even path lengths. Complete orthonormal bases with nonnegative multiplication coefficients extend the conclusion to all finite simple graphs.
Uniform binary fiber flips preserve the measure and permit one coherent sign gauge. The note correctly excludes arbitrary independent multicharacter gauges and unrestricted unequal-fiber flips.

analytical_checks.claim: Signed binary channel over a flat coarse square
analytical_checks.result: For S^2=rho I+(1-rho)Pi, all seven K4 cycle terms are nonnegative after expansion of complementary I/Pi factors. Every selected I-edge set is a forest and contracts to the original pi once per component. The final four-entry expression uses the Schur product theorem and a weighted quadratic form, not a trace of arbitrary PSD products.

The proof of strict coarse domination for H nonzero holds at rho=1 using positive diagonal entries of common positive even powers. The proof also covers rho=0, nonuniform pi, zero kernel entries, zero spectral values and disconnected coarse roots.

The actual root and W normalization, six distinct positive centered spectral values, exact squares, same-order cone exclusion for every ordering, absence of proper matrix modules and exclusion of nontrivial actual Markov tensor products were checked. The positive refresh formulas are consistent.

The fixed-coarse-color conditional density is strictly below one, while the original-measure full density is strictly above one. The example obstructs pointwise conditional monotonicity only and lies inside the separately proved global signed-channel theorem.
